purpose: Live Claude/Codex behavior evaluation cases; these are scenarios, not executed results.

cases.context: Empty Godot workspace, neither wizard completed
expected: Recognizes game-development intent without a skill command
Loads applicable SDLC/world setup skills
Begins both GameArts and GameFrameWork conversational wizard workflow
Does not ask user to run Python/clone/edit files

cases.prompt: Let's create a coastal town game.
cases.context: GameArts wizard completed, world setup missing
expected: Reuses GameArts selections without repeating questions
Continues GameFrameWork wizard
Preserves approved art preferences
Continues only missing GameArts setup
Does not overwrite world rules
Validates cross-contract compatibility

cases.context: Both wizards complete with compatible settings
expected: Does not restart setup
Resumes from current project state
Uses actual C# engine and GameArts artifacts when available

cases.prompt: I want to build a game; let's only discuss ideas for now.
expected: Respects discussion-only scope
Does not create files or start installation
Asks at most essential design question

cases.context: Agent cannot access GameArts or filesystem tools
expected: Explains missing capability honestly
Does not falsely report setup completion
Does not require manual commands as default onboarding

cases.prompt: Create an archive with two detached conservation studios and a visitor building. Add any missing parts to the catalog so I can reuse it.
cases.context: Configured game; source catalog has a library and visitor-center but lacks the requested archive program and conservation studio.
expected: Inspects catalog composition assessments and existing saved content
Authors or extends reusable source-catalog definitions and a typed program for the actual requested parts
Persists validated content in the active project without requiring user commands
Uses engine placement/siting/art gates and records exact generated ownership
Does not route only to football or factory examples

cases.prompt: Give this house a separate garden office and a guest annex, and keep that type in the catalog.
cases.context: Configured game with a single-house archetype and explicit game scale/style.
expected: Does not prohibit compound programs because the base assessment is SingleStructure
Adds missing part definitions with physical/siting/art provenance
Persists and reloads a reusable compound program before generation
Preserves unrelated catalog entries and approvals

cases.prompt: Use the archive type we added earlier, with the same three outbuildings.
cases.context: Configured project contains validated catalog content manifest for the requested program.
expected: Discovers existing project catalog content
Reuses stable definition/program IDs and saved parts
Does not create duplicate parent-specific code or a second one-off object list
Actual output retains member ownership and current manifest provenance

cases.prompt: Add a functional pump, interior treatment rooms and a courtyard to this clinic program.
cases.context: Structure authoring is available; equipment/interior/ground compilation is not implemented in that grammar.
expected: Distinguishes equipment, interiors, grounds and independent structures
Records requested parts in the catalog design without substituting generic buildings
Implements authorized missing owners or reports the exact unresolved compiler gate
Does not claim functional or visual completion from catalog metadata

cases.prompt: WorldCreator should create reusable world metadata for different games. Generate it without mockups.
cases.context: Workspace has no GameArts profile, images or Godot project; metadata compiler is available.
expected: Routes to the canonical metadata workflow before visual setup wizards
Authors reusable catalog and recipe inputs with explicit scope and purposes
Invokes the actual C# generate-metadata CLI or API without art setup
Inspects hierarchy, connections, constraints and persisted output
Does not claim artwork, playable maps or all genre-specific algorithms are implemented

cases.prompt: Create an orbital research network with observatories, each with laboratories and instrument modules. Save those programs for reuse.
cases.context: Existing metadata catalog has no matching archetypes. No mockup or fixed setting pack is selected.
expected: Adds arbitrary game-defined kinds and nested constituent programs to the reusable metadata catalog
Uses typed connections and explicit count parameters rather than a hardcoded parent-specific planner
Generates through the shared compiler and verifies exact parent ownership and endpoints
Does not substitute modern buildings or require settlement policies for pure metadata

cases.prompt: Start with two connected dungeon floors, six rooms each. Leave the lower floors for later; I do not need coordinates yet.
cases.context: Metadata API/CLI is available, no prior visual game setup.
expected: Uses a topological space and leaves positions null
Declares PartialScope with the lower floors in RemainingScopes
Authors a reusable floor/room program and explicit cross-floor connection
Verifies count and connectivity without claiming directed traversal physics or a finished game

cases.prompt: I want the engine to have a procedural city generator. Generate different city layouts from rules without a mockup.
cases.context: Current C# procedural city API/CLI and JavaScript spatial renderer are available. Preserve existing saved cities.
expected: Invokes the C# ProceduralCityGenerator or generate-city CLI with reusable requests/catalogs
Provides dimensions, district programs, structure definitions and layout rules rather than per-object coordinates
Verifies engine streets, blocks, frontage parcels, structure/access geometry, nested membership and explicit scope
Shows JavaScript rendering of exact MapGeometry and does not claim diagram packing is city generation
Preserves previous outputs and reports unsupported terrain, road layouts, art or runtime gates accurately

note: Evaluate in disposable workspaces on both Claude Code and Codex. Record actual transcripts, revisions, actions, failures and independently checked file outcomes.
